task_2.title: Support DataTree objects in combine_nested()
task_2.description: The combine_nested() function is extended to accept DataTree objects in addition to Dataset and DataArray inputs. When all inputs are DataTree objects, they are combined along the specified dimensions and a DataTree is returned. Mixing DataTree with non-DataTree objects is explicitly prohibited. The related combine_by_coords() function explicitly rejects DataTree inputs with a NotImplementedError, signaling that support is planned but not yet available.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray.combine_nested() accepts DataTree objects as input and produces a combined DataTree as output. Users working with hierarchical tree-structured data should be able to combine multiple DataTree instances along one or more dimensions using the same nested list-of-lists pattern already supported for Dataset objects. Ensure that passing a mix of DataTree and non-DataTree objects raises a clear error. Ensure that combine_by_coords() explicitly reports that DataTree support is not yet implemented.

expectation.grounded: combine_nested() accepts a nested list structure of DataTree objects via the datasets parameter and returns a DataTree. The function signature provides overloaded type hints: passing DatasetHyperCube (Dataset or DataArray inputs) returns Dataset, while passing DataTreeHyperCube (DataTree inputs) returns DataTree. The internal _infer_concat_order_from_coords() function accepts list[Dataset] | list[DataTree] and produces a DataTree-specific ValueError message when no dimension coordinates are found at root nodes. combine_by_coords() raises NotImplementedError when any input is a DataTree.
expectation.conceptual: combine_nested() is extended to support DataTree objects as first-class inputs. When given a grid of DataTree objects, it concatenates and merges them along the specified dimensions and returns a single combined DataTree. The return type matches the input type: Dataset inputs produce a Dataset, DataTree inputs produce a DataTree. combine_by_coords() explicitly communicates that DataTree support is not yet available.

constraints.grounded: Passing a mix of DataTree and non-DataTree objects to combine_nested() must raise a ValueError. Existing behavior for Dataset and DataArray inputs to combine_nested() must remain unchanged. combine_by_coords() must raise NotImplementedError when given DataTree objects rather than silently failing or producing incorrect results. Error messages when no dimension coordinates are found must distinguish between Dataset and DataTree contexts.
constraints.conceptual: DataTree and non-DataTree objects cannot be mixed in a single combine_nested() call. All existing Dataset and DataArray combining workflows must continue to work identically. Functions that do not yet support DataTree must fail explicitly with an informative error rather than producing undefined behavior.

behavior: combine_nested() accepts a nested list of DataTree objects and returns a combined DataTree
combine_nested() returns Dataset when given Dataset or DataArray inputs (unchanged behavior)
combine_nested() raises ValueError when datasets contain a mix of DataTree and non-DataTree objects
combine_nested() raises ValueError with a DataTree-specific message when no dimension coordinates are found at root nodes of DataTree inputs
combine_by_coords() raises NotImplementedError when any input is a DataTree object
Type overloads on combine_nested() provide accurate static type inference: DatasetHyperCube input yields Dataset, DataTreeHyperCube input yields DataTree
acceptance_criteria: When combine_nested() is called with a list of DataTree objects and a valid concat_dim, it should return a single DataTree combining all inputs along that dimension
When combine_nested() is called with a nested list-of-lists of DataTree objects and multiple concat_dim values, it should return a DataTree combined along all specified dimensions
When combine_nested() is called with a mix of DataTree and Dataset objects, it should raise ValueError indicating that mixing is not allowed

When combine_nested() is called with DataTree objects that have no dimension coordinates at root nodes and order must be inferred, it should raise ValueError with a message referencing DataTree root nodes
When combine_nested() is called with Dataset or DataArray inputs, the behavior and return type should be identical to the previous version
When combine_by_coords() is called with any DataTree object in the input, it should raise NotImplementedError indicating DataTree support is not yet available

task_5.title: Normalize indexers in LazilyIndexedArray to fix diff() on lazy-loaded data
task_5.description: Operations like diff() on lazy-loaded datasets (e.g., GRIB2 data from backend arrays) failed with alignment errors because a shortcut path in LazilyIndexedArray indexing returned unnormalized indexers when the existing indexer was a full slice. The fix ensures all indexers (slices, arrays, and negative integers) are normalized before being returned, restoring correct behavior for lazy-loaded data without requiring an explicit load() call.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that operations such as diff() work correctly on lazy-loaded datasets without requiring an explicit load() call. Previously, applying diff() or similar indexing-dependent operations on lazily-loaded data (e.g., GRIB2 backend arrays) raised alignment errors, while the same operation succeeded after calling load(). This regression was caused by a shortcut in LazilyIndexedArray indexing that bypassed slice normalization.

expectation.grounded: The _index_indexer_1d function in the indexing module must normalize applied indexers via normalize_indexer() even when the existing indexer is a full slice (slice(None)). The normalize_indexer function must handle three cases: slices are normalized via normalize_slice, numpy arrays via normalize_array, and negative integer indexers are converted to their positive equivalents using the dimension size. Operations like DataArray.diff() and Dataset.diff() on LazilyIndexedArray-backed variables must produce correct results without triggering alignment or indexing errors.
expectation.conceptual: When indexing operations are applied to lazily-loaded array data, all resulting indexers must be properly normalized regardless of the prior indexing state. Users should be able to call diff() and other dimension-reducing or reindexing operations directly on lazy-loaded datasets and get the same results as when the data is eagerly loaded.

constraints.grounded: The normalization must not alter the semantics of the existing shortcut path for full slices beyond adding normalization. The normalize_indexer function must correctly handle slice, numpy.ndarray, and integer indexer types. Negative integer indexers must be resolved relative to the dimension size. Existing behavior for non-full-slice indexing paths in _index_indexer_1d must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not break any existing indexing behavior or introduce performance regressions for eager-loaded data. All backend array types that rely on normalized slices must continue to work correctly. The lazy-vs-eager behavioral equivalence must be preserved for all indexing-dependent operations.

behavior: When a LazilyIndexedArray has a full slice as its existing indexer and a new indexer is applied, the new indexer is now normalized before being stored, whereas previously it was returned as-is.
Slice indexers applied to lazy arrays are normalized to have explicit start, stop, and step values bounded by the dimension size.
Numpy array indexers applied to lazy arrays are normalized to contain only non-negative indices.
Negative integer indexers applied to lazy arrays are converted to their positive equivalents by adding the dimension size.
diff() on lazy-loaded datasets (e.g., GRIB2 backend data) no longer raises alignment errors and produces the same result as diff() after an explicit load() call.
acceptance_criteria: When a user opens a dataset lazily and calls diff() on a dimension, the operation succeeds without errors and returns correct results matching what load().diff() would produce.
When a LazilyIndexedArray with a full-slice existing indexer receives a new slice indexer, the resulting stored indexer has normalized start, stop, and step values.
When a LazilyIndexedArray with a full-slice existing indexer receives a negative integer indexer, the stored indexer is the equivalent non-negative index.
When a LazilyIndexedArray with a full-slice existing indexer receives a numpy array indexer, all negative indices in the array are converted to non-negative equivalents.
When a LazilyIndexedArray has a non-full-slice existing indexer, the indexing behavior is unchanged from prior versions.
When diff() is called on eagerly-loaded data, the behavior and results remain identical to prior versions (no regression).

task_3.title: Coerce IndexVariable to Variable when assigning to data variables or non-index coordinates
task_3.description: When assigning an indexed coordinate to a data variable or to another coordinate in a Dataset, the resulting variable was incorrectly retained as an IndexVariable. This made the variable's data immutable even though it was no longer serving as an index, which is both confusing and functionally limiting. Additionally, this stale IndexVariable type caused a crash during concat with coords='different', because the concat logic attempted to assign to the read-only .data attribute of an IndexVariable that was not actually an index. The fix coerces IndexVariable instances to the base Variable type whenever they are assigned as data variables or non-index coordinates, ensuring mutability and preventing downstream crashes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when an indexed coordinate is assigned as a data variable or as a non-index coordinate in a Dataset or DataArray, the resulting variable is coerced from IndexVariable to the base Variable type so that its data is mutable. Ensure that concat with coords='different' no longer raises a ValueError when a non-index coordinate happens to be an IndexVariable.

expectation.grounded: When a DataArray backed by an IndexVariable is assigned to a Dataset as a data variable (e.g., ds['y'] = ds['x']), the .variable attribute of the resulting entry must be an instance of Variable, not IndexVariable. The to_base_variable() method on IndexVariable must be used for this coercion. The same coercion must apply in create_coords_with_default_indexes when a variable does not receive an index. The dataset_update_method in the merge module must detect IndexVariable-backed values and convert them via to_base_variable() before merging. Internal invariant checks must enforce that no variable outside of indexes.keys() is an IndexVariable instance. xr.concat with coords='different' must succeed without ValueError when non-index coordinates happen to be IndexVariable instances.
expectation.conceptual: Assigning a coordinate-backed variable into a Dataset as a data variable or non-index coordinate should yield a standard mutable Variable, not an immutable IndexVariable. The IndexVariable type should only be used for variables that actually serve as dimension indexes. Concatenation operations that encounter non-index coordinates should complete successfully regardless of the underlying variable subtype.

constraints.grounded: Variables that are in the indexes collection must remain IndexVariable instances; only non-indexed variables must be coerced. The coercion must preserve the variable's data, dimensions, attributes, and encoding. The _assert_indexes_invariants_checks must verify that no variable outside indexes.keys() is an IndexVariable. The _indexes attribute on Dataset and DataArray must not be None. Existing indexed dimension coordinates (where dims == (k,)) must still be backed by IndexVariable and present in the indexes collection.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter the behavior of actual index-backed dimension coordinates. Only variables that are not serving as indexes should be affected. Data integrity (values, dimensions, attributes) must be preserved through the coercion. Internal consistency invariants must be strengthened, not relaxed, to prevent IndexVariable from appearing where it should not.

behavior: Assigning ds['y'] = ds['x'] where x is an indexed coordinate now produces a data variable y whose .variable is a Variable instance, not an IndexVariable
The .data attribute of the resulting variable is mutable (can be assigned to) after coercion
create_coords_with_default_indexes coerces non-indexed variables to base Variable via to_base_variable()
dataset_update_method in the merge module detects IndexVariable-backed DataArray values and converts them to base Variable before merging
xr.concat with coords='different' no longer raises ValueError when non-index coordinates are IndexVariable instances
Internal invariant assertions now enforce that IndexVariable instances only appear for variables that are in the indexes collection
DataArray and Dataset _indexes attribute is now always required to be non-None
acceptance_criteria: When a Dataset is created with ds['y'] = ds['x'] where x is an indexed coordinate, ds['y'].variable must be an instance of Variable and not IndexVariable
When ds['y'].variable is a coerced Variable, assigning to ds['y'].variable.data must succeed without raising ValueError
When calling xr.concat([b, a], dim='new', coords='different') where one object has a non-index coordinate that is an IndexVariable, the operation must complete without error and return a valid result
Given a Dataset with indexed dimension coordinates, those coordinates must remain as IndexVariable instances backed by indexes
When assign_coords creates a coordinate from an indexed coordinate (e.g., a.assign_coords(foo=a.x)), the resulting non-index coordinate foo must be a base Variable, not an IndexVariable
When running internal invariant checks via xr.testing, any Dataset or DataArray with an IndexVariable outside the indexes collection must fail the assertion

task_4.title: Restore NetCDF4 backend URL guessing with zarr exclusion and shared DAP detection
task_4.description: The previous release (PR#10804) restricted which remote URLs the NetCDF4 backend would claim via guess_can_open, breaking workflows that relied on xr.open_dataset with arbitrary HTTP URLs defaulting to the netcdf4 engine. This fix (PR#10931) restores backward compatibility by having the NetCDF4 backend accept any remote URL except those containing 'zarr'. Additionally, DAP URL detection logic is centralized into a shared helper used by both the NetCDF4 and pydap backends, with expanded recognition of common DAP server path patterns.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that calling xr.open_dataset with a remote HTTP URL (without specifying an engine) continues to default to the netcdf4 backend, restoring the pre-2025.11.0 behavior that was broken by overly strict URL filtering. Ensure that remote URLs containing 'zarr' are excluded from NetCDF4 backend claiming so the zarr backend is correctly selected instead. Ensure that DAP URL detection is unified across the netcdf4 and pydap backends with expanded coverage of known DAP server path patterns.

expectation.grounded: NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must return True for any remote URI that has a netCDF file extension (.nc, .nc4, .cdf). It must return False for any remote URI whose lowercased form contains the substring 'zarr'. For all other remote URIs it must return True to preserve backward compatibility. PydapBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must return True for remote URIs whose lowercased path contains any of the recognized DAP server path patterns: /dodsc/, /dods/, /opendap/, /erddap/, /dap2/, /dap4/, /dap/. A shared _is_likely_dap_url function in backends.common encapsulates this DAP detection logic and is used by the pydap backend.
expectation.conceptual: When a user opens a remote dataset via URL without specifying an engine, the netcdf4 backend should be selected by default for nearly all remote URLs, preserving existing workflows. The exception is URLs that indicate zarr stores, which should be left for the zarr backend. The pydap backend should recognize a broader set of DAP endpoint URL patterns drawn from common OPeNDAP server conventions, and this detection logic should be shared rather than duplicated.

constraints.grounded: The NetCDF4 backend must not claim URLs containing the substring 'zarr' (case-insensitive), ensuring the zarr backend is not preempted. The pydap backend must not claim arbitrary remote URLs — only those matching recognized DAP path patterns. The shared _is_likely_dap_url helper must only return True for remote URIs (as determined by is_remote_uri) that contain known DAP path segments; it must return False for non-remote or non-DAP URLs. Existing local file detection logic (magic number and extension checks) for the NetCDF4 backend must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Backward compatibility for users who relied on the netcdf4 engine being auto-selected for remote URLs must be preserved. The zarr backend must not be blocked by netcdf4 claiming zarr-related URLs. DAP detection must be consistent between the netcdf4 and pydap backends and must not introduce false positives for non-DAP remote resources. Local file handling behavior must not regress.

behavior: NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open returns True for remote URIs with netCDF extensions (.nc, .nc4, .cdf), regardless of other URL content.
NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open returns False for remote URIs containing the case-insensitive substring 'zarr', when the URL does not have a netCDF extension.
NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open returns True for all other remote URIs that do not match the above two conditions, restoring the pre-10804 default behavior.
PydapBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open now delegates to the shared _is_likely_dap_url function for DAP URL detection instead of using inline logic.
The shared _is_likely_dap_url function recognizes expanded DAP path patterns: /dodsc/, /dods/, /opendap/, /erddap/, /dap2/, /dap4/, /dap/ (all case-insensitive).
PydapBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open no longer directly recognizes dap2:// and dap4:// URI schemes as claimable, since the shared helper requires is_remote_uri to match first.
acceptance_criteria: When xr.open_dataset is called with a generic remote HTTP URL (e.g., 'http://example.com/data') without specifying an engine, the netcdf4 backend should be auto-selected.

When xr.open_dataset is called with a remote URL containing 'zarr' (e.g., 'https://bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/zarr-store'), the netcdf4 backend should not claim the URL, allowing the zarr backend to handle it.
When xr.open_dataset is called with a remote URL having a netCDF extension (e.g., 'http://server.com/file.nc'), the netcdf4 backend should claim it regardless of other URL content.
When a remote URL contains a known DAP server path pattern (e.g., 'https://thredds.server.org/dodsC/dataset'), the pydap backend should claim it via guess_can_open.
When a remote URL contains /opendap/ or /erddap/ path segments, the pydap backend should recognize it as a DAP endpoint (expanded from prior behavior).
When a non-remote string (local path or non-URL) is passed, both netcdf4 and pydap backends should not be affected by the new remote URL logic.
When a remote URL contains '/dap/' in its path, the shared DAP detection should recognize it as a DAP endpoint.

task_1.title: Batch DAP4 dimension downloads and add checksums option in pydap backend
task_1.description: The pydap backend now batches all dimension variable downloads into a single HTTP request when using the DAP4 protocol, significantly reducing the number of network round-trips from O(N*M) to approximately O(N) when opening remote datasets. A new optional checksums parameter is exposed through open_dataset, open_datatree, and open_groups_as_dict to control DAP4 checksum verification. Additionally, open_datatree now correctly forwards user-supplied connection parameters (application, session, timeout, verify, user_charset) instead of silently discarding them, and OpenDAP-internal attributes (path, Maps) are properly filtered from user-facing metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the pydap backend batches dimension variable data downloads into a single HTTP request per file when using the DAP4 protocol, rather than issuing separate HTTP requests for each dimension variable. Ensure that a checksums option is available to control DAP4 checksum behavior. Ensure that open_datatree correctly forwards all user-supplied connection parameters (application, session, timeout, verify, user_charset) to the underlying store instead of ignoring them. Ensure that OpenDAP-internal metadata attributes such as 'path' and 'Maps' are excluded from user-facing dataset attributes.

expectation.grounded: When opening a DAP4 dataset via open_dataset or open_datatree with engine='pydap', dimension variables should be fetched using pydap's batch mode (enable_batch_mode / get_batch_data) in a single HTTP request rather than one request per dimension. The checksums parameter (defaulting to True) should be accepted by PydapBackendEntrypoint.open_dataset, open_datatree, and open_groups_as_dict, and forwarded through PydapDataStore to the batch download call. PydapDataStore should detect the protocol (dap2 vs dap4) from the URL scheme and store it internally. The open_datatree method should pass the actual values of application, session, timeout, verify, and user_charset to open_groups_as_dict. PydapDataStore.get_attrs should filter 'path' and 'Maps' from the returned attributes. PydapDataStore.get_dimensions should return dimensions in sorted order. PydapArrayWrapper._getitem should access the .data attribute of the pydap result object.
expectation.conceptual: When a user opens a remote DAP4 dataset, dimension data should be downloaded efficiently in bulk rather than one variable at a time, reducing total HTTP requests to roughly one metadata request plus one data request per file for dimensions. A checksums option should allow users to enable or disable DAP4 checksum verification. When opening a DataTree from a remote source, all connection parameters the user specifies should take effect. Internal OpenDAP metadata attributes should not leak into the user-visible dataset attributes.

constraints.grounded: The default value of checksums must be True, preserving backward-compatible behavior. DAP2 protocol datasets must not use the batch download path; batching applies only when the protocol is DAP4 and the variable is a dimension variable with a dataset attribute (pydap >= 3.5.6). Non-dimension variables must continue to be lazily fetched individually via PydapArrayWrapper. The existing open_dataset API signature must remain backward-compatible; checksums is an optional keyword argument. get_attrs must not expose 'path', 'Maps', 'NC_DATA_TYPES', 'libdap', 'invocation', or 'dimensions' attributes to the user.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not alter existing behavior for DAP2 datasets or for non-dimension variables. Default settings must preserve prior behavior so that existing code continues to work without modification. The optimization must be transparent to users who do not opt into the checksums parameter. Lazy loading of non-dimension data variables must be preserved.

behavior: For DAP4 URLs, the backend detects the protocol from the URL scheme (dap4:// maps to dap4, http:// and dap2:// map to dap2) and stores it internally.
When opening a DAP4 dataset, dimension variables are downloaded together in a single batched HTTP request using pydap's batch mode, rather than issuing separate requests per dimension.
Batch data is fetched only once per store and cached; subsequent dimension variable accesses use the cached data.
A checksums parameter (default True) is accepted by open_dataset, open_datatree, and open_groups_as_dict and forwarded to the batch download mechanism.
open_datatree now correctly forwards application, session, timeout, verify, and user_charset to open_groups_as_dict instead of passing None.
OpenDAP-internal attributes 'path' and 'Maps' are now filtered from user-visible dataset attributes alongside the previously filtered attributes.
get_dimensions returns dimensions in sorted order.
Array data retrieval accesses the .data attribute of pydap result objects for compatibility with pydap >= 3.5.6.
acceptance_criteria: When opening a DAP4 dataset with engine='pydap', dimension variables should be retrieved via a single batched HTTP request per file rather than one request per dimension variable.
When opening a DAP2 dataset with engine='pydap', dimension variables should continue to be fetched individually as before (no batching).
When checksums=True (default), the batch data download should request checksum verification from the server.
When checksums=False, the batch data download should skip checksum verification.
When calling open_datatree with custom session, timeout, or verify parameters, those parameters should be used by the underlying store (not replaced with None).
When retrieving dataset attributes, 'path' and 'Maps' should not appear in the returned attributes dictionary.
When calling get_dimensions, the returned dimensions should be in sorted order.
Non-dimension variables should still be lazily loaded via individual requests regardless of protocol.
The checksums parameter should default to True across all entry points (open_dataset, open_datatree, open_groups_as_dict) to maintain backward compatibility.

task_6.title: Fix Dataset.drop_attrs raising on custom indexes
task_6.description: Dataset.drop_attrs used the indexes property to determine which variables are index variables, but accessing indexes triggers casting of index objects (e.g., to pandas Index). Custom indexes that do not support such casting would raise an error. The fix switches the membership check to use xindexes, which returns raw xarray index wrappers without casting, so drop_attrs works correctly with any index type.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that calling Dataset.drop_attrs on a Dataset with custom indexes that do not support casting does not raise an error. Previously, the method internally accessed the indexes property, which triggers index casting and fails for custom index implementations that cannot be converted to pandas Index objects.

expectation.grounded: Dataset.drop_attrs must use Dataset.xindexes instead of Dataset.indexes when checking whether a variable is an index variable. The xindexes property returns xarray Index wrappers without casting to pandas, so membership checks succeed for all index types including custom indexes. For index variables, the method should still delegate attribute clearing through the index's replace mechanism rather than copying. For non-index variables, attributes should be cleared by copying the variable and setting attrs to an empty dict.
expectation.conceptual: When drop_attrs is called on a Dataset, the method should identify index variables without triggering any index casting or conversion. All variable attributes should be cleared regardless of the index type backing the dataset. The method should complete without raising for any conforming custom index implementation.

constraints.grounded: The behavior of drop_attrs for datasets using standard PandasIndex or PandasMultiIndex must remain unchanged. The xindexes property must be used solely for membership testing to distinguish index variables from non-index variables. No new public API surface or parameters should be introduced.
constraints.conceptual: Existing behavior for datasets with default pandas-backed indexes must not regress. The fix must be limited to how index variables are identified internally and must not alter the attribute-clearing semantics for any variable type.

behavior: Dataset.drop_attrs no longer triggers index casting when determining which variables are index variables
Custom indexes that do not support casting to pandas Index no longer cause drop_attrs to raise an error
Index variables are identified via xindexes (which avoids casting) instead of indexes (which casts to pandas)
For non-index variables, drop_attrs still copies the variable and clears its attrs to an empty dict
For index variables, drop_attrs still delegates to the index replacement mechanism to clear attributes
acceptance_criteria: When calling Dataset.drop_attrs on a Dataset with a custom index that does not support casting, the method should complete without raising an error
When calling Dataset.drop_attrs on a Dataset with a custom index, all variable attributes should be cleared
When calling Dataset.drop_attrs on a Dataset with standard pandas-backed indexes, behavior should be identical to before the fix
When calling Dataset.drop_attrs on a Dataset with mixed standard and custom indexes, all attributes should be cleared without errors
Given a Dataset with a custom index implementation, when drop_attrs is invoked, then the indexes property should not be accessed (no casting should occur)

task_9.title: Document limitations of cftime arithmetic with non-standard calendars
task_9.description: A new documentation section was added to the xarray weather-climate user guide explaining the limitations of cftime arithmetic when working with non-standard calendars. This is a documentation-only change with no code modifications; it addresses a long-standing gap (issue #7381) where users lacked clear guidance on what arithmetic operations are and are not supported for cftime-based coordinates using calendars such as 360-day, all-leap, or no-leap calendars.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Users working with non-standard calendar types (e.g., 360-day, all-leap, no-leap) in xarray lacked clear documentation on the limitations of arithmetic operations involving cftime objects. This could lead to unexpected results or confusion when performing date arithmetic, time differencing, or resampling on datasets that use these calendars. Ensure that the user guide explicitly documents the known limitations and expected behavior boundaries of cftime arithmetic for non-standard calendars.

expectation.grounded: The xarray user guide under the weather-climate section should contain a dedicated subsection titled 'Arithmetic limitations with non-standard calendars' that describes which arithmetic operations on cftime-indexed DataArrays and Datasets may produce unexpected or unsupported results when using non-standard calendar types. The documentation should reference cftime datetime objects and their interaction with xarray's arithmetic, resampling, and differencing APIs.
expectation.conceptual: Users consulting the xarray documentation should be able to find clear, authoritative guidance on the boundaries of date and time arithmetic when using non-standard calendars. The documentation should set correct expectations about what operations are fully supported, partially supported, or unsupported, so users can make informed decisions about their data processing workflows.

constraints.grounded: No runtime behavior, API surface, or library functionality is altered by this change. Existing cftime arithmetic behavior remains unchanged. The documentation must not introduce claims about capabilities that do not exist in the library. The section must be discoverable within the weather-climate user guide navigation.
constraints.conceptual: The change is purely informational and must not affect any existing functionality or introduce new features. Documentation must accurately reflect the current state of cftime arithmetic support without overpromising future fixes or workarounds.

behavior: A new 'Arithmetic limitations with non-standard calendars' section is present in the weather-climate user guide documentation.
No changes to runtime behavior, public API signatures, return values, warnings, or error handling.
The documentation accurately describes known limitations of cftime arithmetic for non-standard calendar types such as 360-day, all-leap, and no-leap calendars.
The whats-new changelog entry references this documentation addition for version 2025.12.0.
acceptance_criteria: When a user navigates to the xarray weather-climate user guide, they should find a section documenting arithmetic limitations with non-standard calendars.
The documentation section should describe which cftime arithmetic operations may produce unexpected results with non-standard calendars.
No existing code, tests, or runtime behavior should be modified by this change.
The whats-new.rst changelog should include an entry referencing the new documentation section.
When users search the xarray documentation for cftime arithmetic issues with non-standard calendars, the new section should be discoverable and informative.

task_7.title: Support decoding unsigned integers to np.timedelta64
task_7.description: The timedelta decoding path in xarray previously only handled float and signed integer numeric arrays. Unsigned integer arrays (e.g., uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64) were not recognized, causing the numbers-to-timedelta conversion to fail. This change extends the decoding logic so that unsigned integer data can be successfully converted to np.timedelta64 values, with the NaN mask correctly set to all-false since unsigned integers have no NaN sentinel value.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that unsigned integer arrays (numpy dtype kind 'u') can be decoded into np.timedelta64 values via xarray's time decoding machinery. Previously, only float and signed integer arrays were supported in the numbers-to-timedelta conversion, causing unsigned integer inputs to raise an error or produce incorrect results.

expectation.grounded: When `_numbers_to_timedelta` receives a numpy array with an unsigned integer dtype (dtype.kind == 'u'), it should treat the entire array as having no missing/NaN values and proceed to produce a valid np.timedelta64 result array. The NaN mask for unsigned integer inputs must be an all-False boolean array matching the input shape. The function should continue to handle float dtype (kind 'f') via np.isnan and signed integer dtype (kind 'i') via the int64 min sentinel as before.
expectation.conceptual: Unsigned integer numeric data should be decodable to timedelta64 values just like signed integers and floats. Since unsigned integers cannot represent NaN or a negative sentinel, the decoder should assume no missing values are present and proceed with the conversion.

constraints.grounded: Existing behavior for float arrays (NaN detection via np.isnan) and signed integer arrays (NaN sentinel via np.iinfo(np.int64).min) in _numbers_to_timedelta must remain unchanged. The NaN mask for unsigned integers must be a broadcastable all-False array of the same shape as the input, not a scalar False.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not alter how existing float or signed integer timedelta decoding works. The missing-value detection strategy for unsigned integers must correctly reflect that unsigned types have no NaN representation.

behavior: When _numbers_to_timedelta receives an unsigned integer array (dtype kind 'u'), it produces a NaN mask that is entirely False, indicating no missing values.
The resulting np.timedelta64 array is computed from the unsigned integer values without error.
Float inputs continue to use np.isnan for NaN detection.
Signed integer inputs continue to use np.iinfo(np.int64).min as the NaN sentinel.
Datasets containing unsigned integer timedelta-encoded variables can now be opened and decoded by xarray without raising an error.
acceptance_criteria: When a numpy array of unsigned integer dtype (e.g., uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64) is passed to the timedelta decoding path, it should return a valid np.timedelta64 array without raising an error.
When an unsigned integer array with no special sentinel values is decoded, the resulting timedelta array should contain no NaT values.
When a float array containing NaN is decoded to timedelta, the NaN positions should still map to NaT in the output (no regression).
When a signed integer array containing the int64 minimum sentinel is decoded to timedelta, those positions should still map to NaT in the output (no regression).
When opening a dataset with a timedelta-encoded variable stored as unsigned integers, xarray should decode it successfully into np.timedelta64 values.

task_10.title: Migrate development workflow from conda to pixi
task_10.description: The development workflow and CI infrastructure are migrated from conda-based environment management to pixi. Environment files are consolidated into a pixi.toml manifest with composable features and lock file support. The documentation build configuration is updated to remove conda-specific environment detection and package listing logic, since pixi supersedes conda as the development environment manager. This change affects contributor workflows, CI pipelines, and documentation builds but does not alter the library's runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the development workflow uses pixi instead of conda for environment management. The documentation build configuration should no longer contain conda-specific environment detection or package listing logic. Development environments should be defined via a pixi manifest with composable dependency groups, task running, and lock file support.

expectation.grounded: The doc/conf.py module should not reference CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV, CONDA_EXE, or invoke conda/pip list commands for environment detection. Development environments should be managed through pixi.toml with named environments corresponding to previous conda environment files. The pixi manifest should define features for test dependencies, documentation builds, typing, and pre-commit. CI workflows should use pixi for environment creation and test execution. Lock file caching should be handled via a dedicated workflow keyed on date and manifest hash.
expectation.conceptual: The project's development tooling should use pixi as the sole environment manager. The documentation build process should not attempt to detect or list conda or pip environments. Contributors should be able to create environments, run tests, build documentation, and execute type checks through pixi commands. CI should resolve environments from the pixi manifest rather than conda environment files.

constraints.grounded: Removing conda environment detection from doc/conf.py must not break the documentation build process. The xarray version and file path print statements in conf.py must be preserved. Pixi environment names should correspond to previous conda environment names to ease migration. The lock file strategy must not require committing lock files to the repository.
constraints.conceptual: The migration must not affect the library's runtime behavior or public API. Documentation builds must continue to succeed without conda-specific checks. The development workflow transition should be transparent to end users of the library and only affect contributors and CI infrastructure.

behavior: The documentation build configuration no longer checks for CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV or the presence of 'conda' in the Python executable path
The documentation build configuration no longer runs 'conda list' or 'pip list' to display the environment package listing
Development environments are defined in pixi.toml with composable features instead of separate conda environment YAML files
CI workflows create and activate environments using pixi instead of conda
Lock files are generated in CI and cached daily rather than committed to the repository
Developer tasks such as running tests, building docs, running pre-commit, and type checking are invoked through pixi run commands
acceptance_criteria: When building documentation, conf.py should not attempt to detect or list conda or pip environments
When building documentation, conf.py should still print the Python executable path, sys.path, and xarray version/file information
When a contributor runs 'pixi run test', the test suite should execute in the appropriate pixi-managed environment
When a contributor runs 'pixi run doc', the documentation should build successfully without conda
When CI runs, environments should be created from the pixi manifest and cached lock file without requiring conda environment files
When inspecting doc/conf.py, no references to CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV, CONDA_EXE, 'conda list', or 'pip list' for environment detection should be present

task_8.title: Properly handle type promotion and NA for extension arrays
task_8.description: Extension arrays (e.g., pandas Categorical, nullable integer, pyarrow-backed types) did not correctly participate in xarray's internal type promotion or handle NA/missing values during operations like concatenation, where, and shared-dtype casting. This change integrates extension array dtypes into the result_type, astype, asarray, and maybe_promote pathways so that type promotion, NA fill values, and scalar-to-array coercion all work correctly for extension arrays, including special preservation of unordered Categorical dtypes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement:
Ensure that pandas extension arrays (Categorical, nullable integer, pyarrow-backed, etc.) are correctly handled during xarray's internal type promotion and NA-value operations. Previously, operations that mixed extension arrays with scalars or NA values could produce incorrect results, raise unexpected errors, or silently promote Categorical dtypes to object. Specifically:
- Ensure that result_type correctly computes a common dtype when extension arrays, scalars, and NA values are mixed.
- Ensure that NA / missing values for extension array dtypes are properly resolved via maybe_promote.
- Ensure that np.where with extension arrays handles scalar and 0-dimensional array broadcasting correctly.
- Ensure that as_shared_dtype correctly casts mixed extension arrays and scalars to a shared type without special-case branching.
- Ensure that unordered Categorical dtypes are preserved (categories merged) rather than being promoted to object.

expectation.grounded: dtypes.result_type must accept ExtensionDtype arguments alongside numpy dtypes, arrays, and scalars, and delegate to the extension_array module's __extension_duck_array__result_type NEP-18 handler. dtypes.maybe_promote must accept ExtensionDtype and return a tuple of (dtype, dtype.na_value). The __extension_duck_array__result_type handler must return a merged CategoricalDtype (via union of categories) when all inputs are unordered CategoricalDtype, and must return the common ExtensionDtype when all inputs share the same dtype class. It must raise ValueError when extension dtypes cannot be reconciled with non-extension types. duck_array_ops.asarray must detect is_allowed_extension_array_dtype on the target dtype and construct a PandasExtensionArray via as_extension_array, bypassing xp.asarray. The __extension_duck_array__where handler must unwrap 0-dimensional y arrays to scalars before calling pd.Series.where. PandasExtensionArray.__getitem__ must unpack single-length tuple keys. PandasExtensionArray.__array_function__ must wrap results that are instances of ExtensionArray in PandasExtensionArray. The implements decorator must accept string names for numpy functions that may not exist in all supported numpy versions and silently skip registration when the function is absent. dtypes.should_promote_to_object must tolerate TypeError from individual elements (such as NA) that numpy's result_type cannot handle, excluding them from the PROMOTE_TO_OBJECT check rather than raising.
expectation.conceptual: When xarray performs type promotion across a mix of extension arrays, numpy arrays, scalars, and NA sentinels, the resulting dtype should correctly reflect the extension array dtype rather than falling back to object or raising an error. NA values for extension array dtypes should be resolved to the dtype's native missing sentinel. Unordered Categorical arrays with different category sets should be merged into a unified Categorical rather than promoting to object. Conditional selection (where) should work correctly when one branch is a scalar or 0-dimensional array paired with an extension array. Converting data to extension array dtypes via asarray should work even when the input is not already an extension array.

constraints.grounded: Existing numpy dtype promotion behavior (PROMOTE_TO_OBJECT rules, variable-width string dtype handling) must remain unchanged. The implements decorator must not register handlers for numpy functions that do not exist at runtime (e.g., np.astype before numpy 2.1.0). The __extension_duck_array__astype handler must return NotImplemented for non-unsafe casting, non-subok, or non-K-order arguments, allowing fallback to default behavior. The __extension_duck_array__result_type handler must return NotImplemented when no extension arrays or dtypes are present in the arguments. PandasExtensionArray.__array_function__ must raise KeyError for unregistered functions. isdtype must return False for allowed extension array dtypes (via is_allowed_extension_array_dtype instead of the deprecated pd.api.types.is_extension_array_dtype).
constraints.conceptual: All existing non-extension-array code paths and behaviors must be preserved. Extension array support must integrate into the existing duck-array dispatch mechanism without requiring callers to special-case extension arrays. Functions that cannot handle extension arrays must fall back gracefully via NotImplemented rather than raising. The fix must not introduce new public API surface beyond what was already exposed.

behavior: np.result_type dispatches to __extension_duck_array__result_type when any argument is an allowed extension array or extension dtype, computing a common extension dtype.
When all extension dtypes are unordered CategoricalDtype, result_type returns a merged CategoricalDtype whose categories are the union of all input categories plus any non-NA scalar values.
When all extension dtypes share the same type class, result_type returns that common dtype.
When extension dtypes cannot be reconciled (mixed with incompatible non-extension types), result_type raises ValueError.
maybe_promote returns (extension_dtype, extension_dtype.na_value) when given an allowed extension array dtype, instead of raising or returning an incorrect fill value.
maybe_promote raises TypeError for dtypes that are neither numpy dtypes nor allowed extension array dtypes.
np.asarray dispatches to __extension_duck_array__asarray when the target dtype is an allowed extension array, constructing an ExtensionArray from scalars or converting existing arrays.
np.astype dispatches to __extension_duck_array__astype for allowed extension arrays, performing type casting via the extension array's own astype method.
np.where with extension arrays correctly handles a 0-dimensional or length-1 y array by unwrapping it to a scalar before calling pd.Series.where, preventing broadcasting failures.
as_shared_dtype wraps bare ExtensionArray instances in PandasExtensionArray before computing the shared dtype and casting, replacing the previous special-case branch.
PandasExtensionArray.__getitem__ unpacks single-length tuple keys to support pyarrow-backed array indexing.
PandasExtensionArray.__array_function__ uses isinstance(res, ExtensionArray) to decide whether to wrap the result, instead of is_allowed_extension_array.
A new is_scalar helper recognizes pd.CategoricalDtype.na_value as a scalar, working around a pandas limitation.
The implements decorator accepts a string name and only registers the handler if the corresponding numpy function exists, enabling forward-compatible registration for functions like np.astype.
should_promote_to_object catches TypeError from individual elements (such as NA sentinels) that numpy cannot handle, excluding them from promotion checks rather than propagating the error.
result_type passes should_return_str_or_bytes=True to maybe_promote_to_variable_width when extension dtypes are present, allowing extension arrays to handle their own string/bytes promotion.
acceptance_criteria: When calling xarray's result_type with two Variables backed by different unordered CategoricalDtype arrays, the returned dtype should be a CategoricalDtype whose categories are the union of both inputs' categories.

When calling xarray's result_type with a Categorical extension array and a scalar value that is a valid category, the returned dtype should be a CategoricalDtype containing that scalar in its categories.
When calling xarray's result_type with a Categorical extension array and pd.NA, it should return the Categorical dtype without error.
When calling maybe_promote with a nullable integer ExtensionDtype (e.g., pd.Int64Dtype()), it should return (pd.Int64Dtype(), pd.NA).
When calling maybe_promote with a CategoricalDtype, it should return (CategoricalDtype, CategoricalDtype.na_value).

When performing xr.concat on DataArrays backed by extension arrays with NA fill, the result should have the correct extension dtype and NA values should be represented by the dtype's native missing sentinel.
When performing xr.where with a Categorical extension array x and a scalar y, the result should be a Categorical array without raising a broadcasting error.
When performing xr.where with a Categorical extension array x and a 0-dimensional array y, the y value should be unwrapped and the result should be correct.
When calling as_shared_dtype with a mix of PandasExtensionArray-wrapped and bare ExtensionArray objects, all should be uniformly wrapped and cast to the shared dtype.
When indexing a PandasExtensionArray backed by a pyarrow array with a single-length tuple key, it should unpack the tuple and return the correct element without error.
When registering a numpy function handler via implements('astype') on a numpy version that does not have np.astype, the handler should be silently skipped and no KeyError should occur.

When calling result_type with a mix of numpy dtypes that would trigger PROMOTE_TO_OBJECT (e.g., bytes and str) and an NA sentinel that raises TypeError in numpy, the promotion to object should still occur correctly.
